_about: Hand-written card facts, keyed by NORAD id. 'fact' shows on the card; 'source' is where it was checked; 'stats' can override the third stat. Keep every fact true and checkable. Objects without an entry get a computed fact (see js/lore.js).

25544.title: International Space Station
25544.fact: It’s about the size of a football field and flies at **28,000 km/h**. It could cross Canada in about 12 minutes.

48274.title: Tiangong Space Station
48274.fact: China’s own space station. Its name means **Heavenly Palace**, and astronauts have lived aboard non-stop since 2022.

20580.title: Hubble Space Telescope
20580.fact: About the size of a school bus. Astronauts visited it **five times** to repair and upgrade it in orbit.

16908.title: Ajisai, the mirror ball
16908.fact: Covered in **318 mirrors**. As it spins it throws flashes of sunlight at the ground, so watch for it twinkling.

3597.title: OAO 2 Space Telescope
3597.fact: One of the **first successful space telescopes**, launched in 1968 to study stars in ultraviolet light the atmosphere blocks.

6153.title: Copernicus Telescope
6153.fact: Named after Nicolaus Copernicus, it launched the year before his **500th birthday**. It studied ultraviolet light from stars until 1981.

3669.title: ISIS 1
3669.fact: A **Canadian** satellite from 1969, built to study the upper atmosphere that bounces radio signals around the world.

4327.title: SERT 2
4327.fact: A NASA test of **ion engines**, which push with a gentle stream of charged gas. The idea now flies on deep-space probes.

5.title: Vanguard 1
5.fact: The **oldest human-made object still in orbit**. Launched in 1958, it was the **first satellite with solar power**. Its radio fell silent in 1964.

1573.fact: One of only two Strela-1 test satellites that carried an experimental **nuclear battery** (an RTG) as well as solar cells.

1588.fact: One of only two Strela-1 test satellites that carried an experimental **nuclear battery** (an RTG) as well as solar cells.

18129.fact: A Tsikada navigation satellite that also carried two **ham radio** transponders, RS-10 and RS-11, for radio amateurs to use.

13301.fact: The very first **COSPAS search-and-rescue** satellite. In September 1982 it helped a station in Ottawa find a plane that had crashed in **British Columbia**, and everyone aboard was rescued.

17369.fact: The **first satellite to fly a TOPAZ nuclear reactor**, launched in 1987 to test it together with a new kind of electric rocket engine.

18187.fact: The second of two experimental Soviet satellites that tested the **TOPAZ nuclear reactor** in 1987.

22675.fact: In 2009 this dead relay satellite collided with Iridium 33: the **first accidental collision between two intact satellites**. More than 2,000 pieces of debris were tracked afterwards.

11792.title: Unidentified rocket object
11792.fact: Its **origin is uncertain**. The US catalogue links it to a 1966 Delta launch; independent analysis suggests debris from **Ariane’s first launch in 1979** instead.
